To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common pathogen is Klebsiella pneumoniae, the most common resistance mechanism is extended-spectrum beta-lactamases, the most common antibiotic resistance pattern is resistance to third-generation cephalosporins.

the most common bacteria isolated from ascites patients were Escherichia coli (E. coli), Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) and Klebsiella pneumonia (K. pneumonia), and the most common resistance patterns of the isolated bacteria were to ampicillin, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid and ciprofloxacin.
the most frequent pathogen isolated from ascites patients in intensive care units was Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), and the resistance to antibiotics in S. aureus was high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of antibiotic resistance of pathogens isolated from ascitic fluid patients in ICU.
a study of antibiotic resistant pathogens isolated from ascites patients in the ICU during past 12 year and the analysis of the antibiotic susceptibility.
a comprehensive analysis of the antibiotic resistance patterns and the distribution of the resistant genes of the pathogens isolated from ascites patients in intensive care units.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most common pathogens isolated from ascites fluids are gram-negative bacteria and gram-positive bacteria are isolated in lower numbers.
the use of antimicrobial agents in the intensive care unit is a major factor in the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and the development of nosocomial infections.

the antibiotic resistance of the pathogens isolated from ascites of the ICU patients in China has been increasing, and the resistance of the gram-positive cocci has increased more than that of the gram-negative bacilli, but the resistance of the Enterobacteriaceae is increasing more than that of other gram-negative bacilli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were not able to find any significant difference between the antibiotic resistance rates of the bacteria isolated from the ascites fluid of patients in the intensive care unit and other bacteria.

the antibiotic resistant pathogens are still a serious challenge for the treatment of ascites fluid patients, and it is necessary to strengthen the monitoring and management of antibiotic resistant pathogens in the intensive care unit (ICU).
the antibiotic resistant pathogens isolated from ascites patients in ICU were the main pathogens of nosocomial infections in our hospital.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current methods of antibiotic resistance testing are inadequate for the detection of resistance in some pathogens, and that the use of these methods in clinical settings may lead to inappropriate treatment of infections.
the antibiotic resistance patterns of the pathogens causing infections in the intensive care unit have changed over time, and that this change is not uniform across different species.
we can use a combination of machine learning and network science to identify patients who are likely to be at risk for sepsis.
